newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine resumes T-bill servicing after short delay.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine resumes T-bill servicing after short delay.

text.p: Ukraine's Finance Ministry began paying 3.9 trillion karbovanets ($22 million) in interest and principal on Treasury bills on Thursday, dealers said.
The money, due at the banks late Wednesday or early Thursday, started arriving at 1.30 p.m. (1030 GMT), half a day late, dealers at Bank Ukraina and TK Kredit said.
It was the second time in less than a month that the Finance Ministry had delayed payments by half a day.
Officials at the Finance Ministry would not comment.
The money was owed for a maturing three-month T-bill and quarterly interest on nine-month and 12-month issues.

A spokesman in the central bank's capital markets department said earlier the Finance Ministry had not calculated the amount of money needed to meet the payments properly and had not told the central bank when the payments would be made.
Ukraine is withdrawing the karbovanets currency from circulation by September 16 and replacing it with the hryvnia, but calculations on T-bill transactions are still done in the old currency.

T-bill payments were delayed for half a day in late August and finance ministry officials blamed commercial banks for being late in paying for T-bills bought earlier in the week, which in turn delayed the ministry making its payments.
Bankers were unhappy about the delays.
"The ministry is starting to make a practice of delaying payments," said TK-Kredit banker Serhiy Krushevsky.
Igor Frunze of Finance and Credit bank said banks were losing confidence in the ministry.
The Finance Ministry is due to pay 779.9 billion karbovanets on September 13, 4.1 trillion karbovanets on September 18 and 8.3 trillion karbovanets on September 25.
The central bank plans to raise 150 billion karbovanets this year in T-bill sales to help cover the projected 467 trillion karbovanets budget deficit.
